This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 and 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 SCCH-5 for the relief of compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest.

2. The petition averments briefly stated as under; That on 06.05.2024 at about 1.00 p.m. petitioner was riding his motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-JF- 9066 at Nettigere Gate, Bengaluru - Kanakapura Road, Uttarahalli Hobali, Bengaluru South, Bengaluru, at that time, a rider of Yamaha motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-05-LD-9725 ridden the vehicle at high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against motor cycle of the petitioner.
Due to the impact, petitioner sustained severe injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to General Hospital,
Kaggalipura, after first-aid he was shifted to CURA Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and SCCH-5 spent a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical, nourishment and attendant charges.
3.
At the time of the accident, petitioner was aged about 58 years, hale and healthy, doing tender coconut business, thereby earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is not in a position to day-to-day activities and undergoing deep mental shock, pain and suffering and suffered permanent disability.
With regard to accident in crime No.160/2024 is registered against the rider of the offending motor cycle before the Kaggalipura Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 being the insurer, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence prays to allow the petition and grant compensation.
SCCH-5 4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has not appeared before court hence placed exparte.
Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement and denied averments of the petition.

Further denied issuance of policy to Yamaha motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-LD-9725 vide policy No.33970248624 600000 valid from 14.06.2021 to 13.06.2026 and if there is any liability of this respondent to indemnify respondent No.1 is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further respondent No.2 seeks protection available under Sec.147 and Sec.149(2) of M.V.Act.
Respondent No.2 submitted that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.

Further submitted that, offending Yamaha motor cycle was not at all involved in the alleged accident Muddappa vs Sourabh Biswas on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188763330/
2 and rider of the said motor cycle was not holding valid and effective driving SCCH-5 licence as on the date of accident.
Respondent No.2 denied name, age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. Based on the pleadings of the parties this court has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1. Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 06.05.2024 at about 1.00 p.m. near Nerrigere Gate,
Bengaluru - Kanakapura Road, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru South due to rash and negligent driving of one Yamaha motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-LD- 9725 dashed against the petitioner motor cycle and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
SCCH-5 6.

In order to prove the case, Petitioner himself examined as PW-1, examined Dr.Shailesh A. V.Rao,
Senior Consultant Neurosurgeon at Padmashree Diagnostics as PW-2 and marked 18 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.18 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence.
7. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record and my findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:

::REASONS::
8. Issue No.1:- In order to prove the case, petitioner examined himself as PW-1, in his chief- examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated SCCH-5 in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated.

In order to prove road traffic accident PW-1 produced and marked copy of FIR as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint as Ex.P.2, copy of mahazar as Ex.P.3, copy of IMV Report as Ex.P.4, copy of charge sheet as Ex.P.6,
copy of Sec.133 notice as Ex.P.7, copy of reply as Ex.P.8.
Muddappa vs Sourabh Biswas on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188763330/
3 9.
Further to substantiate the petitioner's case, petitioner has examined Doctor as PW-2.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1, PW-2 and documents those have marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.8 corroborates the case of the petitioner about occurrence of the road traffic accident dated 06.05.2024 as alleged in the petition.

10. Per contra, except filing of written statement, respondent No.2 has not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as SCCH-5 alleged in the petition and to discard the evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, this tribunal held that the petitioner sustained the injuries due to the accident occurred on 06.05.2024 at about 1.00 p.m.
when he was riding motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-JF-9066 at Nettigere Gate, Bengaluru - Kanakapura Road, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru South, Bengaluru.
11.
It is evident from police papers that, very accident is occurred due to negligence of rider of Yamaha motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-LD-9725.
Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
SCCH-5 12. Issue No.2:-

As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained laceration wound over right parietal region, multiple abrasions over B/L cloner limbs, closed head injury with right MCA territory infarct In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.5,
discharge summary marked as Ex.P.9 issued by CURA Hospital, wherein he took treatment as indoor patient from 06.05.2024 to 15.05.2024.

Further he has exhibited OPD Book as Ex.P.10,
medical bills of Rs.2,51,507/- as Ex.P.11.
13.
Further Dr.Shailesh A.V.Rao is examined as PW-2.

To substantiate his evidence, he has exhibited OPD Record as Ex.P.14, CT-Scan Brain Report as Ex.P.15, Neuro Physiological Assessment Report as Ex.P.16, MMSE Report as Ex.P.17, CT-Brain Film and CD as Ex.P.18 and he has assessed neuro disability SCCH-5 pertaining to cognition at 10%.

In cross-examination he has categorically admitted that, he has not consulted any treated Doctor to assess the disability and he is not a member of any District Medical Board and as per the 2018 Gazette Notification, he has assessed the disability at 10%.
further deposed that, as per MRS-1, he has assessed 10% disability and there is a possibility of stroke to the petitioner due to road traffic accident.
Further PW-2 deposed that, there is possibility of stroke to the petitioner due to nicotine dependent syndrome.

Under such circumstances, considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner the functional disability of the petitioner is considered at the rate of 10% i.e.,neuro disability pertaining to cognition, for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.
SCCH-5 14.

As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 58 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.12, wherein it is clearly mentioned year of birth of the petitioner as 1967 and the alleged accident was occurred in the year 2024, accordingly relying on Muddappa vs Sourabh Biswas on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188763330/
4 Ex.P.12

his age is considered about 58 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 9 is applicable as per decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

sentences.text: 15. As per his case, he was doing tender coconut business, thereby earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
To prove the said fact, there are no documents on record.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional SCCH-5 income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.16,500/-
p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As per the evidence of PW-2 he examined petitioner on 06.02.2025 i.e., nearly after 9 months and on examination date as per version of PW-2 and by considering the gravity of injury sustained by petitioner it may take at least 3 months to recover.
For the said SCCH-5 period he is entitled for the loss of income.
As per the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner should be taken into consideration i.e., Rs.16,500/- p.m.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the income of said quantum for the period he was admitted as inpatient in the hospital.
So petitioner is entitled for Rs.49,500/- towards loss on income during laid up period.
17. Further admittedly petitioner has exhibited Ex.P.11 medical bills for Rs.2,51,507/-.
On perusal of the said bills it is clearly stated about spending of amount for this treatment is concerned.
Further on perusal of Ex.P.5 in which Doctor who have treated has categorically stated that, petitioner has sustained grievous injury out of the accident occured on 06.05.2024.
As per Ex.P.5 wound SCCH-5 certificate, petitioner has sustained laceration wound on right parietal region, multiple abrasions over limbs which are grievous in nature.
Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against Shams Shahriar for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.

So the said charge sheet materials and evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 clearly states that, petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.
18.
Per contra except denial in the written statement, respondent No.2 has not taken any endeavors to step into witness box nor proved the allegations as alleged in the written statement.

In the absence of rebuttal evidence, merely respondent No.2 has filed written statement and they have denied entire case of the SCCH-5 petitioner are all not sufficient to disbelieve the petitioner case.
19. Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-

Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
Muddappa vs Sourabh Biswas on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188763330/
5 1. Loss of Future Income 1,78,200-00 2. Pain and sufferings 25,000-00 3. Conveyance, nourishment and 15,000-00 attendant charges 4.
Medical Expenses 2,51,507-00 5. Loss of amenities in life 15,000-00 6. Loss of income during laid up 49,500-00 period Total 5,34,207-00 20.
Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,34,207/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.
SCCH-5 21

. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.33970248624600000 which is valid for the period from 14.06.2021 to 13.06.2026, the alleged accident was occurred on 06.05.2024 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Hence naturally liability of respondent No.1 shall go against respondent No.2, so that,
respondent No.2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
within 60 days from the date of this order.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.

22. Issue No.3: For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
SCCH-5

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,34,207/- (Rupees Five Lakhs Thirty Four Thousand Two Hundred Seven Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
Muddappa vs Sourabh Biswas on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188763330/
6
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

2025)
